chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slave and the polytheist: do they block (the heirs) if they do not inherit? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.إِذَا لَمْ يَرِثَا: If they do not inherit (dual form)
key_terms.اَلْمَمْلُوكِ: The slave (male or female), a specific category in classical inheritance law
key_terms.اَلْمُشْرِكِ: The polytheist, one who associates partners with God

ai.seo_question: Do slaves or polytheists block heirs from inheriting in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a slave (*mamluk*) and a polytheist (*mushrik*) are excluded from inheritance (*hajb*) because they do not inherit themselves, a ruling derived from the principle that non-inheriting entities cannot block heirs. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence to differentiate between those who are merely excluded from the estate and those who actively prevent others from receiving their share, contrasting with the specific blocking rules applied to non-Muslim spouses. The hadith underscores the Shia interpretation of Quranic verses where 'blocking' is contingent upon the blocker's own eligibility to inherit.
